problem: All manifolds are connected and compact. Write dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Use genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives. For a smooth real (1,1) form theta, PSH(X,theta) means theta+dd^c u>=0. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C and equivalence means mutual order, including the canonical values at common poles. Extended products mean non-pluripolar Monge-Ampere products with smooth-background corrections. A big background admits a genuine strict current theta+dd^c u>=epsilon h for some Hermitian h and epsilon>0. BMP means v_+(h)<infinity, where v_+(h) and v_-(h) are the supremum and infimum of integral(h+dd^c u)^n over all bounded h-psh u. Positive lower mass means v_-(h)>0; it is distinct from BMP. Define I(tu) by local integrability of |g|^2 exp(-tu), with no extra factor 2. Ideal equivalence means equality at every real t>0. P_theta[u]_I is the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=0 ideal-equivalent to u. P_theta[u] is the ordinary singularity envelope, the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=0 with v preceq u. The lower and upper singularity volumes are the infimum and supremum of the extended mass over all v ordinarily equivalent to u in the specified background, not the raw mass of one representative. Fix a smooth big theta on X without BMP and real a<c. For every smooth positive Hermitian eta, let (Gamma_tau^eta)_(tau<c) be genuine normalized ideal-model potentials in background theta+eta, pointwise concave and decreasing in tau and constant for tau<=a. Require compatibility Gamma_tau^eta=P_(theta+eta)[Gamma_tau^(eta prime)]_I whenever eta>=eta prime. All slices have supremum zero. For any fixed Hermitian h, the decreasing limit Gamma_tau=lim_j Gamma_tau^(h/j) exists, is genuine and an ideal model in theta, and is independent of h. Recovery asks Gamma_tau^eta=P_(theta+eta)[Gamma_tau]_I for every eta and every finite tau<c. Original P19 asks for an invariant and uniform estimates forcing this recovery beyond BMP, with correct behavior on modifications, and recovering the positive limiting lower-volume theorem when BMP holds. Known background: projection/retraction give the greatest realizable system below the original system. Recovery is equivalent to survival of the original ideal data, or of every local divisorial Lelong number, in the limit. This equivalence alone is not the desired new sufficient condition. Under BMP, positivity of the initial limiting lower volume suffices: a finite upper-volume deficit gives stretches with uniformly controlled divisorial errors, and concavity propagates positivity to each finite slice. A zero-volume ruled-surface system already fails recovery in a Kahler background. Smooth gauge transport by theta prime=theta+dd^c f and Gamma prime=P_(theta prime)[Gamma-f]_I preserves recovery. Raw initial Monge-Ampere mass need not be gauge invariant in nonclosed backgrounds. No replacement invariant, proposed estimate, nonrecovering family or proof is supplied.
completionCriteria: Construct a substantive sufficient recovery criterion valid without BMP and prove recovery at every finite slice, its modification behavior and the specialization to the known positive lower-volume theorem under BMP. Demonstrate a nonvacuous genuinely unbounded-upper-mass case. Alternatively resolve a substantive obstruction to such an extension with a complete actual envelope-system example. Merely assume ideal survival or recovery itself, use gauge transport as a survival proof, or invoke a finite upper-volume deficit where upper mass is infinite does not answer the question. Keep any restricted result scoped and independently reconstruct it with exact primary-source hypotheses.
